statements.claim: Uddhava, recalling the years at Dwaraka, remembered the host of Kala, the armies of Magadha led by Jarasandha, and Shalva coming against the city, and how each siege was broken when Krishna went out to meet the besiegers.
statements.evidence: BP 3.3.9: 'kāla-māgadha-śālvādīn anīkai rundhataḥ puram' (the hosts of Kala, Magadha and Shalva that besieged the city he slew); pack excerpt: Uddhava recalls how Krishna destroyed these besieging hosts; Jarasandha as Magadha's king is the pack's listed character.

statements.claim: Jarasandha's hatred of the house of Yadu had followed Krishna from Mathura and could not be ended even by defeat.
statements.evidence: Not itemized in BP 3.3.9-10; connective characterization consistent with the corpus-wide Jarasandha-Yadu feud (Mathura sieges, Gomanta) and the pack's framing of Magadha as besieger.

statements.claim: Krishna slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others; some he struck down himself, others he caused to be slain.
statements.evidence: BP 3.3.10: 'śambaraṃ dvividaṃ bāṇaṃ muraṃ balvalam eva ca...' plus the pack's rendering 'he killed, or had killed' (Dantavakra among 'others like' the named); excerpt: 'slew Shambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala, Dantavakra and others.'

statements.claim: Shambara fought with illusion; Dvivida was the great ape of the mountains; Bana was the thousand-armed king of Sonitpura.
statements.evidence: One-line identifying epithets not expanded in BP 3.3.10 but matching the standard tradition used across this corpus (Dvivida as vānara in BP 10.67; Bana thousand-armed lord of Sonitpura; Shambara famed for māyā). Non-contradictory descriptors within a recalled name-litany.

statements.claim: Behind Krishna stood the strength of Dwaraka — Balarama with his plough and the warriors of the Yadu clan.
statements.evidence: Framing of the Yadava defence; consistent with the pack's arena (Dwaraka defences) and Balarama's role as Dwaraka's champion elsewhere in the corpus; not a specific sourceable assertion in 3.3.9-10.

statements.claim: Dwaraka stood whole after the sieges, and the women on the walls trusted their king, watching without weeping when he rode out.
statements.evidence: Atmospheric aftermath describing the city that would not fall; the pack states only that Krishna slew/defeated the besiegers, so the city's survival is the implied outcome.

notes: Close rendering of BP 3.3.9-10 (Uddhava's recall). All names and the killed-or-caused-to-be-slain distinction match the verse. Epithets and siege atmosphere are connective and non-contradictory. No issues.

statements.claim: Balarama went to Vraja alone, with Krishna's consent.
statements.evidence: HV 1.102: 'Rāma, recollecting his friendship with Gopas, alone went to Vraja with Krishna's consent.'

statements.claim: On reaching Nanda's cow-pens he was embraced by the gopas and gopis, who were overjoyed at his return.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.1: 'pariṣvaktaś cirotkaṇṭhair gopair gopībhir eva ca' (embraced by gopas and gopis who had long yearned for him).

statements.claim: The cowherd elders welcomed Balarama, saying they had heard of his deeds: destroying the great fish Panchajana in the ocean, fighting Jarasandha and the kings with him at Gomanta, and entering Mathura by which the earth was steadied.
statements.evidence: HV 1.102.12-15: 'We have heard of thy encounter, in the ocean, with Timi-like Panchajana, of his destruction and thy battle with Jarāsandha and other Kshatriyas on Gomanta... Thy entrance into the city of Mathura... By it the earth has been established.'

statements.claim: Balarama told the cowherds they were dearer than his own kin, that he and Krishna were reared in their houses, took meals with them, tended the cattle, and spent boyhood sporting there — they were firm friends.
statements.evidence: HV 1.102.17-19: 'You are our better friends than even the Yādavas. We had been reared by you and spent our boyhood in sporting here. We took our meals in your houses and tended the kine. You all are our firm friends.'

statements.claim: The gopis asked whether Krishna remembered his father, mother and friends, and complained that he had left them suddenly, cutting the thread of friendship; they wondered how the wise ladies of Dwaraka could trust the words of one so quick to charm and quick to leave.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.9-12: 'kaccit smarati vā bandhūn pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca saḥ... tā naḥ sadyaḥ parityajya gataḥ sañchinna-sauhṛdaḥ... kathaṃ nu gṛhṇanty anavasthitātmano vacaḥ kṛta-ghnasya budhāḥ pura-striyaḥ.'

statements.claim: When one gopi tried to turn the talk to other subjects the rest rejected it, saying their hearts were still with Krishna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.13: 'kiṃ nas tat-kathayā gopyaḥ kathāḥ kathayatāparāḥ' (what use to us, gopis, of other tales?).

statements.claim: Balarama consoled the gopis with Krishna's heart-felt messages, assuring them Krishna remembered his father, mother, boyhood friends and nights of song by the Yamuna.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.15: 'saṅkarṣaṇas tāḥ kṛṣṇasya sandeśair hṛdayaṃ-gamaiḥ' (Balarama [consoled] them with Krishna's heart-reaching messages); the enumerated content mirrors the gopis' questions (10.65.9-11) and the pack summary ('consoled the gopis... with Krishna's heart-felt messages').

statements.claim: Balarama stayed in Vraja for two months, the spring months of Madhu and Madhava, sporting with the gopis in the Yamuna groves under the full moon with flower-scented winds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.16-17: 'dvau māsau tatra cāvātsīn madhuṃ mādhavaṃ eva ca / pūrṇa-candra-kalā-mṛṣṭe kaumudī-gandha-vāyunā'; pack summary: 'he stayed two months, sporting with them in the Yamuna groves.'

notes: Faithful blend of BP 10.65.1-17 and HV 1.102; speeches (elders' praise, Balarama's reply) closely track HV's wording, gopis' questions and Krishna's messages track BP. No issues.

statements.claim: The goddess Varuni, sent by Varuna, flowed out of the hollow of a tree, and the fragrance of the honey-stream was carried to Balarama by the wind.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.18-19: 'varuṇa-preṣitā devī vāruṇī vṛkṣa-koṭarāt / taṃ gandhaṃ madhu-dhārāyā vāyunopahṛtaṃ balaḥ.'

statements.claim: As he drank, gandharvas sang, drums sounded in the sky and flowers rained down; women sang his deeds.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.20-22: 'upagīyamāno gandharvair vanitā-śobhi-maṇḍale / nedur dundubhayo vyomni vavṛṣuḥ kusumair mudā / upagīyamāna-carito vanitābhir halāyudha.'

statements.claim: Intoxicated, Balarama wore a single earring and a garland, his blue cloth loose, eyes rolling with pleasure — like the moon of an autumn night.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.23: 'sragvy eka-kuṇḍalo matto vaijayantyā ca mālayā'; HV 1.102.22-29: 'Clad in an apparel dark-blue like a cloud... eyes rolling in intoxication... enjoy there like the moon in an autumnal night.'

statements.claim: Balarama summoned the Yamuna to come in bodily form and sport with him in her waters.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.24: 'sa ājuhāva yamunāṃ jala-krīḍārtham īśvaraḥ'; HV 1.102.30: 'O great river, going to the ocean... come to me therefore in your bodily form.'

statements.claim: The Yamuna did not come — disregarding his words as the outcome of drunkenness — and he called again, 'Will you not come?'
statements.evidence: HV 1.102.31: 'Yamunā disregarded his words as being the out-come of drunkenness and did not come'; VP 5.25: 'calling out, Will you not come... will you not come?'

statements.claim: Enraged, Balarama drove the point of his plough into the river's bank and dragged her; the currents were upset and the fishes and water creatures grew bewildered as the river was forced from its course.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.25: 'anāgatāṃ halāgrena kupito vicakarṣa ha'; HV 1.102.34-35: 'Bāma began to drag the bank... the currents of the river were upset and all the fishes and the aquatic animals grew bewildered'; VP 5.25: 'compelled the dark river to quit its ordinary course.'

statements.claim: Frightened, the Yamuna begged pardon: 'Rama, Rama, mighty-armed, I did not know your valour — forgive the river that did not know the glory of the Blessed One.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.26-28: 'evaṃ nirbhartsitā bhītā yamunā yadu-nandanam / rāma rāma mahā-bāho na jāne tava vikramam / paraṃ bhāvaṃ bhagavato bhagavan mām ajānatīm.'

statements.claim: His anger left him; he released the Yamuna, bathed and sported in her waters, and came out wearing blue garments and a golden garland.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.29-31: 'tato vyamuñcad yamunāṃ yācito bhagavān balaḥ / kāmaṃ vihṛtya salilād uttīrṇāyā... vasitvā vāsasī nīle mālāṃ āmucya kāñcanīm.'

statements.claim: Long afterward the cowherds pointed to the path where the river had been dragged, and the night passed like a single moment.
statements.evidence: BP 10.65.32-33: 'adyāpi dṛśyate rājan yamunākṛṣṭa-vartmanā / evaṃ sarvā niśā yātā ekeva ramato vraje.'

notes: Follows BP 10.65.18-33 with supporting color from HV 1.102 and VP 5.25; the summons, refusal, dragging, plea and release all track the sources. Vivid similes are connective. No issues.

statements.claim: Dvivida was an ape, the friend of Narakasura, who wrought destruction on the land in requital for his slain friend.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.2-3: 'sakhyuḥ so 'pacitiṃ kurvan vānaro rāṣṭra-viplavam'; pack summary: 'Dvivida, the mighty ape and friend of Narakasura, seeking vengeance.'

statements.claim: Narakasura had been slain by Krishna.
statements.evidence: VP 5.36 (cross-ref in pack cluster): Dwivida 'vowed to revenge... the destruction of Naraka by Krishńa'; consistent with the corpus's Narakasura-slaying cluster.

statements.claim: Dvivida set fire to cities and villages.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt (BP 10.67.1-8): 'set fire to cities and villages...'; VP 5.36: 'he set fire to the forests, to villages, and to towns.'

statements.claim: He tore up mountains by their roots and crushed the regions below, stood mid-ocean and flung up the sea with his arms so the coastal lands drowned.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.3-4: 'kvacit sa śailān utpāṭya tair deśān samacūrṇayat / kvacit samudra-madhya-stho dorbhyām utkṣipya taj-jalam'; pack excerpt: 'uprooted mountains, drowned the coastal lands.'

statements.claim: He defiled the hermitages of the sages, breaking their trees and scattering their offerings and sacred fires, and hurled men and women into mountain caves.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.5-6: 'āśramān ṛṣi-mukhyānāṃ kṛtvā bhagna-vanaspatīn / puruṣān yoṣito dṛptaḥ kṣmābhṛd-dronī-guhāsu saḥ'; pack excerpt adds 'defiled the sages' hermitages and sacred fires.' (Scattered offerings = connective gloss of defilement.)

statements.claim: He devastated the regions, defiling women of good families.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.7: 'evaṃ deśān viprakurvan dūṣayaṃś ca kula-striyaḥ.'

statements.claim: The land he ravaged was Anarta, the country of the Yadavas.
statements.evidence: Pack index entry lists locations: Anarta for this event; BP 10.67.8 places Balarama, lord of the Yadus, at the scene of the devastation.

statements.claim: In the midst of the ruin Dvivida came upon Balarama, the lord of the Yadavas, standing with a garland of lotuses around his neck — not Krishna, who had slain his friend, but the other brother.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.8: 'tatrāpaśyad yadu-patiṃ rāmaṃ puṣkara-mālinam' (there he saw Rama, the Yadu lord, garlanded with lotuses); Balarama as plough-bearer and Krishna as Narakasura's slayer are the pack's cluster facts.

notes: Renders BP 10.67.1-8 accurately (event evt_0255); Dvivida's motive, ravages and the closing face-off with lotuses-garlanded Balarama all match. Terror-atmosphere sentences are connective. No issues.

statements.claim: Balarama was drinking varuni wine in the groves of Raivataka hill in the company of women, singing, when the ape Dvivida came and climbed onto a branch overhead.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.9-10: 'gāyantaṃ vāruṇīṃ pītvā mada-vihvala-locanam / duṣṭaḥ śākhā-mṛgaḥ śākhām ārūḍhaḥ kampayan drumān'; VP 5.36: 'Halāyudha was drinking in the groves of Raivata, along with the illustrious Revatī and other beautiful females.'

statements.claim: Dvivida had been the dearest friend of Narakasura, whom Krishna slew, and in grief and fury had sworn to make the world pay.
statements.evidence: VP 5.36 (in pack): Naraka 'had a friend of exceeding prowess in the monkey named Dwivida... vowed to revenge... the destruction of Naraka by Krishńa.'

statements.claim: Dvivida had interrupted sacrifices, subverted rites, set fire to forests/villages/towns, hurled rocks on cities, cast mountains into the ocean, churned the sea over its shores, assumed shapes at will, enlarged himself to crush harvests, and deprived the land of peace and sacred study.
statements.evidence: VP 5.36 (in pack), recounting the ape's ravages verbatim: interrupted rites, 'set fire to the forests, to villages, and to towns,' overwhelmed cities with rocks, 'lifted up mountains... cast them into the ocean,' agitated the sea over its confines, 'could assume what shape he would, enlarged his bulk... crushed and spoiled the harvests,' and the world 'was deprived of sacred study and religious rites.'

statements.claim: The ape mocked Balarama and the women — grinning, rolling his eyes, flicking his brows and making faces at them until they drew back.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.11-12: 'tā helayām āsa kapir bhrū-kṣepair sammukhādibhiḥ'; VP 5.36: 'grinned at and mocked him, and laughed at the women.'

statements.claim: Balarama hurled a stone at him; the ape caught it and laughed, mocking him further.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.13-14: 'taṃ grāvṇā prāharat kruddho balaḥ... gṛhītvā helayām āsa dhūrtas taṃ kopayan hasan.'

statements.claim: Balarama took up his mace and plough; the ape struck him on the head, and the blow fell as harmlessly as red chalk flung at a mountain.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.16-19: 'kruddho muṣalam ādatta halaṃ cāri-jighāṃsayā... tena balaṃ mūrdhany atāḍayat... girir yathā gairikayā prahāraṃ nānucintayan.'

statements.claim: Balarama struck him with the mace, blow after blow, until the ape's body was broken in a hundred places.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.20: 'tenāhanat su-saṅkruddhas taṃ balaḥ śatadhācchinat.'

statements.claim: The ape kept fighting, hurling a rain of trees and rocks that fell harmlessly; Balarama cast aside his weapons and seized him with his bare arms, and when he brought him down the earth with its mountains and forests trembled.
statements.evidence: BP 10.67.22-25: 'tato 'muñcac chilā-varṣaṃ balasyopari... yādavendro 'pi taṃ dorbhyāṃ tyaktvā muṣala-lāṅgale / cakampe tena patatā sa-ṭaṅkaḥ sa-vanaspatiḥ'; pack excerpt adds 'after hurling trees and rocks in vain.'

statements.claim: The ape lay felled, vomiting blood, and did not rise; cries of victory and homage sounded in the sky and the gods rained flowers.
statements.evidence: Pack excerpt: 'was felled, vomiting blood, as gods rained flowers'; VP 5.36: 'felled him, vomiting blood, and lifeless'; BP 10.67.26: 'jaya-śabdo namaḥ-śabdaḥ sādhu sādhv iti cāmbare.'

statements.claim: Afterward the villages Dvivida had burned were at peace again, and the hill of Raivataka was said to carry a scar where the ape fell.
statements.evidence: The restored-land aftermath is implied by the slaying (BP 10.67.27 'nihatya dvividaṃ jagad-vyatikarāvaham' — slaying the ape who afflicted the world); the specific 'scar on the hill' is a folk-style close attributed to 'they said afterward,' not stated in the pack.

notes: Accurate to BP 10.67.9-27, with the ravages-recap drawn from VP 5.36 as the pack intends; follows the BP variant (mace + bare-arm finish, per variant note 'BP: fells with mace') rather than VP's single fist-blow, which is the allowed variant choice. No issues.

statements.claim: Samba, a prince of the Yadava house, lay captive among the Kurus, and the young warriors of Dwaraka had girded for war; Balarama pacified them.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.13: 'sāntvayitvā tu tān rāmaḥ sannaddhān vṛṣṇi-puṅgavān'; pack summary: the Kauravas hold and refuse to release Samba; HV 1.119 (cluster): 'Shāmva was confined by those princes in the city of Hastina.'

statements.claim: Balarama set out alone for Hastinapura in a chariot radiant as the sun and, arriving at the city of the elephants, stopped in the outer grove rather than riding in.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.14-15: 'jagāma hāstina-puraṃ rathenāditya-varcasā / gatvā gajāhvayaṃ rāmo bāhyopavanam āsthitaḥ.'

statements.claim: Dhritarashtra (son of Ambika), Bhishma, Drona and Bahlika received him gladly with the cow of welcome and water of honor and asked after his kinsmen's welfare.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.16-19: 'so 'bhivandyāmbikā-putraṃ bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ ca bāhlikam / te 'ti-prītās... gām arghyaṃ ca nyavedayan / bandhūn kuśalinaḥ śrutvā pṛṣṭvā śivam anāmayam.'

statements.claim: Balarama delivered the message of Ugrasena, king of the Yadavas: the Kurus had seized one righteous man by many, unjustly, and should release Samba.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.20-21: 'ugrasenaḥ kṣiteśeśo yad va ājñāpayat prabhuḥ / yad yūyaṃ bahavas tv ekaṃ jitvādharmeṇa dhārmikam.'

statements.claim: The Kauravas, led by Duryodhana and his brothers, mocked the Yadavas as upstarts bound to the Kurus by marriage, eating at their tables and sleeping under their roofs, whose royal insignia were a gift not a right — 'enough of the Yadavas' kingship'; the claims, they said, fit them like nectar fits a serpent.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.24-26: 'ete yaunena sambaddhāḥ saha-śayyāsanāśanāḥ / cāmara-vyajane śaṅkham ātapatraṃ ca pāṇḍuram / alaṃ yadūnāṃ naradeva-lāñchanair dātuḥ pratīpaiḥ phaṇinām ivāmṛtam'; pack summary: mocked them 'as cowherds who had risen above their station.'

statements.claim: The Kurus asked how even Indra could stand against them while Bhishma, Drona and Arjuna were their champions, and refused to release Samba.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.27: 'katham indro 'pi kurubhir bhīṣma-droṇārjunādibhiḥ'; pack summary: 'the Kauravas... refused' to release Samba.

statements.claim: Balarama saw the Kurus' wickedness and understood that these evil ones, swollen with manifold pride, would not choose peace.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.29-30: 'dṛṣṭvā kurūnāṃ dauḥśīlyaṃ śrutvāvācyāni cācyutaḥ / nūnaṃ nānā-madonnaddhāḥ śāntiṃ necchanty asādhavaḥ.'

statements.claim: Balarama reflected on the glory of Ugrasena — lord of the Bhojas, Vrishnis and Andhakas, before whose feet fortune herself waits and on whose feet the guardians of the world set their crowns — and on the Kurus' taunt that 'the Vrishnis eat land given by the Kurus'; he thought: alas for men mad with wealth, stumbling like drunkards.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.33-38: 'nograsenaḥ kila vibhur bhoja-vṛṣṇy-andhakeśvaraḥ... yasya pāda-yugaṃ sākṣāc chrīr upāste 'khileśvarī / yasyāṅghri-paṅkaja-rajo 'khila-loka-pālair mauly-uttamair dhṛtam... bhuñjate kurubhir dattaṃ bhū-khaṇḍaṃ vṛṣṇayaḥ kila / aho aiśvarya-mattānāṃ mattānām iva māninām.'

statements.claim: Balarama rose and walked out past the elders without another word, carrying his anger with him, unwilling to answer mockery with steel then.
statements.evidence: The packs record the embassy, the mockery and (next beat) Balarama's enraged plough-dragging of the city (BP 10.68.39+; VP 5.35); the silent departure is connective bridging between the two beats and contradicts no pack statement.

notes: Faithful to BP 10.68.13-38; the Kauravas' mockery, the 'nectar to serpents' gibe, the Indra taunt and Balarama's reflections all track the verses, including the pāṇḍuram cāmara/chatra insignia detail folded into 'royal insignia... by gift.' Departure line is connective. No issues.

statements.claim: Still enraged after being mocked, Balarama drove the blade of his plough deep into the earth beneath the ramparts of Hastinapura and declared he would make the earth free of the Kauravas.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.39-40: 'adya niṣkauravaṃ pṛthvīṃ kariṣyāmīty amarṣitaḥ / lāṅgalāgreṇa nagaram udvidārya gajāhvayam'; VP 5.35: 'plunged the blade of his ploughshare downwards, beneath the ramparts of the city.'

statements.claim: The city of Hastinapura — the city of the elephant — tilted, swayed and slid toward the Ganga like a boat torn loose, about to plunge into the river.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.41: 'jala-yānam ivāghūrṇaṃ gaṅgāyāṃ nagaraṃ patat' (the city, whirled like a boat on the water, was about to fall into the Ganga).

statements.claim: The Kurus came out with their families, terrified, and took refuge at Balarama's feet, crying 'Rama, Rama, support of all, we did not know your power; you are the one cause of creation, preservation and destruction; you bear the earth on your head, O thousand-headed one; your anger is for the instruction of the world, not from hatred or envy; homage to you, soul of all beings.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.42-47: 'tam eva śaraṇaṃ jagmuḥ sa-kuṭumbā jijīviṣavaḥ / rāma rāmākhilādhāra prabhāvaṃ na vidāma te / sthity-utpatty-apyayānāṃ tvam eko hetur nirāśrayaḥ / tvam eva mūrdhnīdam ananta līlayā bhū-maṇḍalaṃ bibharṣi sahasra-mūrdhan / kopas te 'khila-śikṣārthaṃ na dveṣān na ca matsarāt / namas te sarva-bhūtātman.'

statements.claim: The Kauravas surrendered Samba and with him Lakshmana, the bride for whose sake the trouble had begun.
statements.evidence: Pack summary: 'the Kauravas, terrified, surrendered Samba and Lakshmana'; HV 1.119: Duryodhana 'sent Shamva with his wife'; VP 5.35: 'the Kauravas delivered Śámba and his bride'; HV 1.119: Samba was confined 'on account of his stealing away Duryodhana's daughter Lakshmanā.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana gave a herd of elephants every one sixty years old and six thousand golden chariots blazing like the sun.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.49-50: 'duryodhanaḥ pāribarhaṃ kuñjarān ṣaṣṭi-hāyanān / rathānāṃ ṣaṭ-sahasrāṇi raukmāṇāṃ sūrya-varcasām.'

statements.claim: Duryodhana asked to be taken as Balarama's pupil in club-fighting, and Balarama accepted him.
statements.evidence: HV 1.119: Duryodhana 'presented himself for his discipleship. Rāma too accepted the Kuru king as his disciple in club fighting.'

statements.claim: Balarama accepted the gifts, released the city, returned to his own city, and in the assembly of the Yadus told his kinsmen the whole tale of what he had done among the Kurus.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.51-52: 'pratigṛhya tu tat sarvaṃ bhagavān sātvatarṣabhaḥ / tataḥ praviṣṭaḥ sva-puraṃ halāyudhaḥ... sametya bandhūn anurakta-cetasaḥ... śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ yadu-puṅgavānāṃ madhye sabhāyāṃ kuruṣu sva-ceṣṭitam.'

statements.claim: Hastinapura was said to have leaned toward the river ever since, never standing quite straight again — a mark the city still shows.
statements.evidence: BP 10.68.53: 'adyāpi ca puraṃ hy etat sūcayad rāma-vikramam' (even today this city exhibits Rama's prowess); HV 1.119: 'from that time, this whirling city is seen bent towards the ocean.'

notes: Accurate to BP 10.68.39-53 with HV 1.119 and VP 5.35 corroboration; the surrender speech, Duryodhana's gifts and discipleship, the assembly retelling and the still-leaning city all match. Tilted-streets panic detail is connective. No issues.

statements.claim: Hearing of the coming war between the Kurus and the Pandavas, Balarama bathed at Prabhasa, gratified the gods, seers and ancestors, and visited the holy waters Prithudaka, Bindu-saras, Tritakupa and Sudarshana and the tirthas along the Yamuna and Ganga.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.16-19: 'śrutvā yuddhodyamaṃ rāmaḥ kurūṇāṃ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ / snātvā prabhāse santarpya devarṣi-pitṛ-mānavān / pṛthūdakaṃ bindu-saras tritakūpaṃ sudarśanam / yamunām anu yāny eva gaṅgām anu ca.'

statements.claim: He came to the Naimisha forest, where the sages were holding a long sacrifice that ran on season after season.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.20: 'tam āgatam abhipretya munayo dīrgha-satriṇaḥ'; Naimisha per pack index/title.

statements.claim: The sages honored Balarama, seated him with his company, and made him welcome.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.21: 'so 'rcitaḥ sa-parīvāraḥ kṛtāsana-parigrahaḥ.'

statements.claim: In the assembly sat Romaharshana, a suta of the charioteer line born of a mixed (pratiloma) union, seated among the brahmanas on a seat of honor; he did not rise nor offer folded hands, though he had been a pupil of the blessed seer Vyasa and had learned much.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.22-24: 'apratyutthāyinaṃ sūtam akṛta-prahvaṇāñjalim / yasmād asāv imān viprān adhyāste pratiloma-jaḥ / ṛṣer bhagavato bhūtvā śiṣyo 'dhītya bahūni ca'; pack excerpt names him Romaharshana.

statements.claim: Balarama judged the suta untamed, undisciplined and vainly proud of his scholarship, seated above the brahmanas in the seat the sages had given him.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.23-25: 'yasmād asāv imān viprān adhyāste... adāntasyāvinītasya vṛthā paṇḍita-māninaḥ'; the seat was the sages' gift per 10.78.29: 'asya brahmāsanaṃ dattam asmābhir.'

statements.claim: Balarama said, 'This is the very purpose for which I was born into this world,' plucked a single blade of kusha grass, and struck the suta down; Romaharshana fell and did not rise.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.26-27: 'etad-artho hi loke 'sminn avatāro mayā kṛtaḥ / etāvad uktvā bhagavān nivṛtto 'sad-vadhād api'; pack excerpt: 'strikes him down with a blade of kusha grass.'

statements.claim: The sages cried out 'Ha! Ha!' in grief and told Balarama: 'We ourselves gave him this seat and raised him to the brahmana's seat; what you have done was done without knowledge — you have slain a brahmana; this is brahma-hatya.'
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.28-30: 'hāheti-vādinaḥ sarve munayaḥ khinna-mānasaḥ / asya brahmāsanaṃ dattam asmābhir yadu-nandana / ajānataivācaritas tvayā brahma-vadho yathā'; pack excerpt: 'the sages cry out that he has committed the sin of slaying a brahmana, saying this was done without knowledge and must be expiated.'

statements.claim: The sages asked Balarama, as purifier of the worlds, whether there is any purifier of this sin, and offered to show him the way to it.
statements.evidence: BP 10.78.31: 'yady etad-brahma-hatyāyāḥ pāvanaṃ loka-pāvana' (the verse continues into the sages' prescription, which the corpus's next story, DKS_0359, records: slay Balvala, then a year-long pilgrimage).

notes: Accurate to BP 10.78.15-31 (event evt_0272): pilgrimage route, the seated suta Romaharshana, the kusha-grass slaying, the sages' 'ha ha' cry and the brahma-hatya accusation all track the pack. Inner-voice details are connective. No issues.
